brief: It rains on this town and the water never leaves the roofs. A grep of the whole source finds no gutter, no downpipe, no eave drip and no runoff anywhere: the roofs are the top third of every wide frame and the largest sloped surface in the picture, they DARKEN when wet (drawSlateCell and drawRoofRow both mix on wetF), and nothing carries a drop off them. Give the houses their rainwater goods — a gutter line along the eave and a downpipe down the face, placed off the geometry that already exists rather than a new list, and let them do something: on a wet day the eaves drip and the pipes run; on a dry day the town gains a vertical rhythm on a hundred facades that it has never had. Then CONNECT it, which is the half that makes this worth an iteration: PUDDLES[] and pudHollow[] already stand water on the pavement off the GRID, and the foot of a downpipe is where a puddle belongs — bias the hollow there rather than adding a new puddle source. Read the traps first: roofs are EMERGENT from buildVolumes(), so read eaveFor()/roofZE() and change no footprint; a FACE is drawn only where the SOUTH neighbour is open, so a pipe on any other side will never be seen; and both the facades and the ground are CACHED, so a static pipe registers at cache time while a running one is a live overlay.
successLooksLike: At the shipping size, on a dry day the facades read with a regular vertical accent they did not have; in rain the eaves are visibly running, and the pavement under a pipe holds water sooner than the pavement beside it. Quote the wet-day diff's mass as a ratio to a same-code control, quote it at the SHIPPING size, and show the dry-day frame is not cluttered.
avoid: Do not change a footprint or a roof height — the roofs are emergent and the law is explicit. Do not add a per-drop particle system; this is fabric, and the rain already has stepDrops(). Do not create a second puddle source: bias pudHollow, do not bypass it. Do not put pipes on the near block's slates without checking nearScale — at NEAR_SZ 1.95 anything drawn there is twice the size it is across the lane.
